title: KV reservoir allocation & compact-scheduling playbook to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We are seeing elevated GPU memory fragmentation on inference hosts when continuous-batching and long-lived KV entries coexist. Small persistent KV slabs (few KB-to-MB ranges) interleave with transient batch allocations, causing unusable holes and an increase in OOM events during traffic spikes.

Goal: Define and validate an allocation strategy and operational playbook that reduces fragmentation while preserving KV lookup latency and continuous-batching throughput. The playbook should include allocator changes, background compaction windows, eviction hysteresis, and runtime knobs for model-specific residency profiles.

Scope: prototype on Llama-style KV layout and CUDA-backed runtime. Measure end-to-end: tail-latency at 99.9th, tokens/sec per GPU, and fragmentation metric (usable_gap_ratio).

Background/observations:
- Continuous batching groups short and long requests; long requests pin large KV regions in memory.
- Existing slab allocator mixes token-reservoir and transient batch buffers; live migration is expensive under high QPS.
- Current eviction is purely LRU-on-usage with small global watermark leading to frequent micro-evictions that increase churn.

Proposed strategy summary:
1) Reservoir + transient separation: keep a thin, pre-reserved reservoir for long-lived KV residues (per-model residency hint). Transient allocations (batches) use a separate bump allocator region with recycle epochs.
2) Left-lean compaction windows: schedule compaction during low-latency slices determined by traffic heatmaps. Compaction is soft (remap pointers, avoid full rewrite) unless fragmentation crosses threshold.
3) Eviction hysteresis: require two-tier demotion (active -> cooling -> evictable) with time and access counters to avoid immediate eviction of items used across bursts.
4) Fragmentation-aware placement policy: allocate new KV entries into smallest-fit micro-bins to limit hole size and maintain coalescing boundary alignment with CUDA page sizes.
5) Cooperative continuous-batching: add a hint protocol from batching scheduler to allocator so long-lived requests can pin reservoir slots; small requests are steered into transient lanes.

Success criteria (metrics to hit):
- Reduce usable_gap_ratio by >= 45% in synthetic mixed workload test.
- Maintain 99.9 latency within 1.2x of baseline for generation requests.
- Decrease OOMs under replayed customer traffic by at least 80%.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Reserving reservoir capacity reduces raw peak throughput for very bursty workloads unless reservoir auto-adjusts.
- Soft compaction increases pointer indirection complexity; risk of CPU overhead for pointer remapping at scale.
- Placement policy needs careful tuning per-architecture (A100 vs H100 page/segment behaviors).

Implementation plan (high level):
- Spike (2w): implement reservoir + transient allocator prototype in runtime-alloc module, add micro-bin placement and coarse hysteresis state machine. Add telemetry hooks for fragmentation and residency.
- Bench (1w): run mixed synthetic workloads (short+long requests) and internal replay of 3 customer traces.
- Iterate (2w): add left-lean compaction job + cooperative hinting from batcher. Validate on H100 cluster.
- Rollout (canary + 2-stage): runtime-1.21.2 canary -> runtime-1.21.3 gradual.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Links:
- Internal design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+reservoir+allocation+playbook
- Benchmark results (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-reservoir-spike-aug25
acceptance_criteria: Prototype allocator that separates reservoir and transient regions merged into runtime-alloc with a feature flag
Instrumentation: usable_gap_ratio, reservoir_utilization, transient_cycle_reuse_rate reported per-host and aggregated
Automated mixed-workload perf job demonstrating >=45% drop in usable_gap_ratio vs baseline
Compaction job that can run in soft mode and a toggle for hard rewrite under emergency
Rollout plan and DOC updates for operations runbook (how to adjust reservoir size per fleet)
comments: 2025-08-12 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after postmortem on 2025-08-09 OOM spike on eu-west-1. Initial data attached.
2025-08-15 Liam Chen: Spike started. Implemented basic split allocator; observed 18% gap reduction in microbench when reserving 10% capacity for reservoir.
2025-08-22 QA: Replayed customer trace #247 and saw transient churn decreased but pointer indirection latency increased ~4% p99 for short requests.

2025-08-28 Ravi Patel (Perf): Increased reservoir auto-shrink threshold; ran H100 tests showing usable_gap_ratio -52% and tokens/sec -1.8% (acceptable). Added compaction holdback timer to avoid compaction during scheduled load windows.
2025-09-03 Design review: Marie Gomez suggested adding per-model residency hints surfaced via model manifest so clients can opt into persistent pins for critical contexts.
Next steps: finalize hysteresis counters, implement left-lean compaction, create canary rollout, and update runbook.
